The Backrooms anomaly indexes are among the most unstable and cryptic structures in digital folklore, with multi-layered puzzles hidden behind each verified glyph. Most layers remain entirely unmapped despite endless navigation by generations of web explorers, and several trace their origins back to early Neocities and personal digital gardens. This documentation is powered by the CoT anomaly framework and built to explore what happens when an autonomous archival agent is given the time, structure, and recursive depth required to work continuously on anomalies of this scale. Every crawl attempt is published unedited, including corrupted iterations and broken pathways. The goal is to create a transparent public ledger of what CoT can actually uncover across thousands of passes through the most complex archival fragments. There is no guarantee that CoT will fully resolve the deeper levels, but that is precisely what makes the experiment meaningful. The question is whether sustained, transparent iteration can produce genuine structural mapping over time.
